groups.title: the local readfirst command: argument parsing, git file listing, init/prompt/check/read/diff and the agent brief

checks.why: init, check, prompt, read and diff end to end on a scratch git repository

risks.text: src/action.mjs imports repoFiles, readMapFile and readText from cli.mjs, so changing how files are listed or the map is read also changes the GitHub Action
repoFiles lists untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude, so a stray scratch file in the working tree makes `check` fail and shows up in `diff`

parse() treats every --option except --json, --help, --force, --agent, --install, --dry-run, --strict, --verify, --stop and --ci as taking a value, so a new on/off flag must be added to that list or it swallows the next argument

`check` reports map problems and exits 1. prompt goes through loadMap and throws (exit 2 from bin) on any map problem. read and diff use loadMapLenient: they only note on stderr when the map is behind the code (files in no group, patterns for deleted files) and still throw when the map is broken in itself (mapProblems with placement: false)
the pattern syntax in the agent brief must match what map.mjs accepts; if you change the pattern rules, update the brief as well

runHook swallows every error and returns null (exit 0, no output), so a bug in it looks the same as 'nothing to say' and the edit goes ahead; only a test with real map data would catch it. It also uses repoFiles, readMapFile and mapProblems, so changes there change the hook

verify runs the map's check commands with the shell in the repository root; a map is repository content and its commands run with the user's rights, so verify stays an explicit command, never called from the PreToolUse hook or the Action. The one exception is the opt-in Stop hook (`hook --install --verify`), and it runs only commands the base branch's map already lists (trustedRuns): a command a branch adds or changes is named, never run, so checking out someone's branch cannot run their new command

the MCP server answers by calling main() again with --root for each tool call, so anything a command prints to stdout becomes the tool's text; stdout is also the JSON-RPC channel, so `mcp` itself must never write anything else to stdout. `mcp` is handled before main() looks up the repository (so it starts outside a git repository): it must not use root, files or the map itself, and the repository is looked up at each tool call (--root, or git rev-parse in the current directory), where a failure comes back as an isError result 'not inside a git repository'

groups.title: the GitHub Action: one PR comment with the read list for the changed files, and a failed check when the map falls behind

checks.why: the Action against a fake GitHub API: post, update in place, broken map, read-only token, non-PR events, auto-fix commits

risks.text: composite actions do not set INPUT_* env vars, so action.yml maps each input to an env var by hand; a new input needs a line in action.yml and a read in action.mjs
the existing PR comment is found by its first line (MARKER); changing MARKER makes every open PR get a second comment instead of an update
a 403 from a comment write is treated as a fork PR and swallowed by matching ': 403 ' in the message built by api(); changing that error text turns fork PRs into failed jobs
the script runs only when argv[1] ends with '/src/action.mjs', and action.yml calls it by that path; moving or renaming the file makes the Action exit successfully without doing anything
when the map has problems the comment shows the problems but no read list, and the job fails unless fail-on-map-problems is 'false'

auto-fix writes to the PR branch through the contents API: only on a branch of this repository (never a fork), only when the branch's map equals the one this run read (else it would overwrite a newer push), and only what settleMap settles; anything a person must decide stays in the comment

groups.title: the map format and checker, the first-draft map, import reading (JS/TS, Python and seven more languages) and the read list

checks.why: patterns, draft, check messages, imports and read list cases

risks.text: mapProblems rejects unknown fields, so a new map field must be added to the allowed-field list and made optional, and older readfirst versions will reject maps that use it; maps in users' repositories must keep passing under readfirst/map@1
the read list object is the --json output and what the Action renders; keep its field names and the readfirst/read-list@1 format string
patternToRegExp is used for group files, ignore, rule files and risk files alike; changing what a pattern matches moves files between groups in every user's map

test files are recognised by two separate regexes (isTest in readlist.mjs, which covers every language langs.mjs reads, and the top-level tests-folder check in draftMap); a new test naming convention goes into isTest, and into draftMap only if it is a top-level folder

imports are read with regexes: JS/TS and Python in imports.mjs, Go, Rust, Elixir, C#, Java/Kotlin, Ruby and PHP in langs.mjs. Only edges that resolve to a tracked file count (workspace packages and tsconfig paths aliases included), so packages from outside, aliases set up elsewhere (bundler config, tsconfig extends), Python code under a source root other than the repository root, `src/` or a folder holding `manage.py`, and names the approximation misses (Rails constants used unqualified inside a module, C# types reached without a using, Python 2 implicit relative imports in a file with no Python 2 syntax) leave tests out of the read list

readlist.mjs and settleMap (map.mjs) read fixMap's change messages (`groups.<id>: added <pattern>`): readlist for the 'would add it to group' hint, settleMap to tell a new top-level folder from a file beside placed ones; rewording those messages silently breaks both

labels are personal: they live in .readfirst/local/, which keepLocal adds to .git/info/exclude; reading labels from anywhere else, or writing them into the map, would hand one person's notes to the whole team
the view page loads three.js 0.160.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net through an import map; without network it shows only the WebGL/connection notice

the view page only has interface strings for en and ko, and the language switch only toggles between them: a labels file for any other language (e.g. `prompt --labels ja`) is read and inlined but never shown, and the plain/technical switch appears only when the current language's file has "plain"

check, read, diff, verify and the Action settle a map that is only behind the code the way fix would (settleMap) and pass; only what fix cannot place, broken rules and new top-level folders fail. Making them strict again breaks every PR that adds a file

the Python folder lookup (`import utils` finding the `utils.py` next to the file) runs only for files that look like Python 2 (print statement, `except E, e:`, `raise E, msg`, `<>`, backquotes) and never with `from __future__ import absolute_import`; applying it to every file links `import logging` or `import jwt` to a same-named local module

groups.title: node:test suites for the command, the map, imports, the read list and the Action

risks.text: npm test only runs test/*.test.mjs, so a test in a subfolder or with another file name never runs
the CLI tests create and commit to real git repositories in the temp folder, so git must be on PATH
fakeGitHub answers any write it does not recognise with success, so a new GitHub API call in action.mjs passes unless a test asserts it
the tests assert exact markdown strings and draft group ids, so rewording toMarkdown or changing draftMap means updating these assertions and the README example
the hook test calls main(['hook']) without a stateDir, so it writes to the real temp folder and relies on a unique session_id; reusing a fixed id would make the hook print nothing on later runs

groups.title: package manifest, README, license and CI

risks.text: package.json "files" decides what npm ships (bin, src, README.md); a new folder under src ships automatically, a new top-level folder the command needs must be added there
CI's readfirst job runs this checkout's own Action (uses: ./), so every PR fails when a new file is not in .readfirst/map.json or when src/action.mjs is broken
the README repeats the command list, the Action inputs table and a sample read list; update it when cli.mjs HELP, action.yml inputs or toMarkdown output change

server.json lists readfirst in the official MCP Registry (mcp-registry.yml, after a release is published and npm shows the version); its version and packages[0].version must equal package.json's version (and package-lock.json's two version fields: run `npm install --package-lock-only` after bumping), and its name must equal package.json's mcpName, or the release or the listing fails (bump all three together)

groups.title: example maps for public repositories, with sample read output

risks.text: each example names the commit it was made at; regenerate the sample output when the read format changes

rules.rule: the readfirst command reads only the checkout: no network calls, no model calls, no API key
rules.why: it runs in agents' sandboxes and on private code; only the Action talks to the GitHub API

rules.rule: no runtime dependencies: Node's standard library only
rules.why: npx readfirst must start fast and nothing third-party runs on users' code

rules.rule: every tracked file is in exactly one group or in ignore, and every group and rule pattern matches a tracked file; check fails otherwise
rules.why: this is what stops the map from quietly falling behind the code

rules.rule: maps written for readfirst/map@1 keep passing: never rename or remove a map field or make an optional one required without a new format version
rules.why: map.json files live in users' repositories and CI fails on any map problem

rules.rule: the read list JSON keeps its field names under readfirst/read-list@1
rules.why: agents and tools read `readfirst read --json` and `diff --json`

rules.rule: only `readfirst init`, `readfirst fix`, `readfirst hook --install` and `readfirst view` write files in the checkout: init writes the map (never over an existing one without --force) and, with --agent, one line in the agent notes, and with --ci .github/workflows/readfirst.yml (never over an existing one); fix writes only the map; hook --install writes only .claude/settings.json and keeps what is already there; view writes only under .readfirst/local/ (the page) and adds one line to this clone's .git/info/exclude, never anything git tracks; the plain `hook` writes only a state file in the temp folder; `hook --stop` writes nothing itself and runs only the base branch's check commands, like verify; check, prompt (with or without --labels), read, diff and the mcp server never change the checkout; verify writes nothing itself and only runs the commands the map lists, which may write as they would when run by hand; the Action writes nothing in the checkout, and with auto-fix only commits the map that fix would write to the PR branch through the API
rules.why: agents run read and diff freely before every change, and the hook runs before every edit, so it must not touch the working tree

rules.rule: the Action keeps a single comment per PR and updates it in place on each push
rules.why: a new comment on every push floods the PR

rules.rule: a read-only token (PR from a fork) must not fail the Action: the read list goes to the job summary instead
rules.why: contributors from forks would otherwise get a red check they cannot fix

rules.rule: the Action takes the PR's changed files from the GitHub API, not from git history
rules.why: actions/checkout defaults to a shallow clone, so any checkout depth must work

rules.rule: the public code holds no hosted-version logic: the prompts and steps that fill the map stay on the server
rules.why: the free code is MIT and public; the paid value is the server's judgement. The hosted design lives in the private readfirst-cloud repository.
